gloss: to nitpick; to be fussy about details

definitions.gloss: to nitpick; to be fussy about details; to split hairs
definitions.explanation: To point out or complain about small, trivial matters. Often used with a mildly negative nuance, implying that the person is being overly particular or pedantic about things that don't really matter.

examples.japanese: そんな{細|こま}かいことを{言|い}わないで。
{彼|かれ}はいつも{細|こま}かいことを{言|い}うので、{周|まわ}りから{嫌|きら}われている。
examples.english: He's always nitpicking, so people around him don't like him.

examples.japanese: {細|こま}かいことを{言|い}うようだけど、{書類|しょるい}の{日付|ひづけ}が{間違|まちが}っているよ。
examples.english: I don't mean to nitpick, but the date on the document is wrong.

notes:
A common set phrase built from {細|こま}かい (detailed, fine) + こと (things) + を + {言|い}う (to say). The expression is used both to criticize someone for being overly particular and as a self-deprecating hedge when pointing something out oneself.

The hedge pattern {細|こま}かいことを{言|い}うようだけど... (I don't mean to nitpick, but...) is very common in workplace settings and polite conversation when one needs to raise a minor issue without seeming difficult.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {細|こま}かいことを{言|い}わないで: don't nitpick
- {細|こま}かいことを{言|い}うようだけど: I don't mean to nitpick, but...
- {細|こま}かいことばかり{言|い}う: to always nitpick
- {細|こま}かいことを{言|い}い{出|だ}す: to start nitpicking

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {口|くち}うるさい: nagging; fussy — describes a person who habitually criticizes
- {重箱|じゅうばこ}の{隅|すみ}をつつく: to poke at the corners of a stacked box — to nitpick obsessively (more emphatic)
- {些細|ささい}なことにこだわる: to fixate on trivial matters — neutral phrasing
